lede: Gilmer is the Upshur County seat, straight up Highway 300 from our Longview shop. We handle lawns, beds, sod, drainage, patios and Christmas lights in town and out on the county roads.
intro: Yard Dog Landscapes is a family-owned landscaping and lawn care company in Longview, and Gilmer is part of our service area in Upshur County. Owner Miller Maines started the company in 2017 and still walks every property himself. The crew is Miller plus four, the same faces every visit, with no subcontractors. We are fully insured and have a 5.0 rating from {{REVIEWS}} Google reviews. Send a quote request any time for a free walkthrough and a written, itemized estimate, usually within a day.

Gilmer sits in sandy country. Upshur County is known for sweet potatoes, which is what the East Texas Yamboree celebrates every October, and the loose, sandy ground that grows them drains fast and holds little water or fertilizer. Lawns here dry out quickly in a July dry spell, and beds need organic matter worked in to hold moisture between rains. Older lots in town tend to have big shade trees. Outside town, along US 271 and the county roads, homes often sit on acreage with pines along the edges and a lot of open, sunny ground.

From Longview, Gilmer is an easy run up Highway 300, so it works for both installs and ongoing maintenance. We walk every property before we price it, because a half-acre in town and five acres off a county road are not the same job. If you are not sure whether your address is in range, send it with a quote request and ask.

yard_notes.title: Sweet potato sand
yard_notes.text: Much of the ground around Gilmer is loose sand that drains in hours. Lawns go dry fast in summer, so mowing tall and watering deep and less often matters more here than in heavier soil.

yard_notes.title: Fertilizer slips through
yard_notes.text: Sandy soil does not hold nutrients long. Slow-release feedings spread across the season beat one heavy application that washes past the roots.

yard_notes.title: Rolling ground washes
yard_notes.text: Upshur County is rolling country, and bare sand on a slope cuts gullies in a hard rain. Groundcover, mulch and a well-placed swale keep the soil where it belongs.

yard_notes.title: Clay under some low spots
yard_notes.text: Sand on top does not always mean a yard drains. Where a clay layer sits underneath, low spots still hold water after a long rain, so we check before assuming.

faq.q: Do you service Gilmer and the rest of Upshur County?
faq.a: Yes. Gilmer is straight up Highway 300 from our shop in Longview, and Upshur County is part of our service area along with Gregg, Harrison, Smith, Rusk, Panola and Nacogdoches counties. If you are out toward Ore City or East Mountain, send the address with a quote request and we will confirm.

faq.q: How much is lawn mowing in Gilmer?
faq.a: Weekly mowing for a typical residential yard starts at $65 a visit. Bigger lots and acreage cost more, and we price those after walking the property, since fence lines, outbuildings and long drives add trim time. You get a flat per-visit price in writing before we start.

faq.q: Can you fix a sandy lawn that will not stay green?
faq.a: Often, yes. Sandy lawns brown out fast because water and nutrients drain through quickly. We raise the mowing height, test the soil, and set up slow-release feedings timed for East Texas. If the turf is too thin to come back, new sod over prepped soil with compost worked in is the reset.

faq.q: Do you do Christmas lights in Gilmer?
faq.a: Yes, and most homes start at $900. We supply the lights, custom-cut professional C9 lines to your roofline, take them down after the season and store them. Booking opens in early October, the same month as the Yamboree, and the install calendar fills up from there.

service_angles.lawn-maintenance: Gilmer lawns on sandy ground dry out fast, and a low cut makes it worse. We mow Bermuda around two to two and a half inches in summer and St. Augustine at three and a half to four, keep the blades sharp, and blow clippings back into the turf, where they return a little moisture and nitrogen. Weekly mowing starts at $65 a visit for a typical yard.
service_angles.leaf-removal: Between the oaks, pecans and pines around Gilmer, fall cleanup is not a one-weekend job. We mulch the light October drop back into the lawn, which feeds organic matter into the sand, then switch to full cleanup and haul-off once the November drop covers the grass, with a last pass before spring green-up since post oaks hang on to leaves into February. Leaf removal is quoted after a walkthrough.
service_angles.fertilization: Gilmer's sandy ground does not hold onto fertilizer, so one heavy feeding mostly washes past the roots. We use slow-release product spread across the season, starting in late April once nights hold above 60 degrees, and aeration helps lawns that have packed down under traffic. Fertilization starts from about $190 per visit.
service_angles.hedge-trimming: Country homes around Gilmer often have long hedge lines along a drive or fence, and those take a different approach than a foundation shrub. We shape long runs of ligustrum, holly or wax myrtle so the base stays wider than the top and light reaches the bottom branches. Most hedge jobs run $150 to $800, depending on length and how overgrown they are.
service_angles.tree-shrub-care: On acreage around Gilmer, the trees and shrubs closest to the house matter most: dead lower limbs shading the lawn, crepe myrtles that got topped, and shrubs swallowing the porch. We prune for structure in the dormant season, thin crepe myrtles instead of topping them, and remove small trees and shrubs that have outgrown their spot. This work is quoted after a walkthrough.
service_angles.tree-planting: Open lots around Gilmer have room for shade trees that most town lots do not, and a live oak or Shumard oak on the west side of the house pays off for decades. In deep sand we pay extra attention to watering the root ball through the first summer, and we plant October through February when we can. Tree planting is quoted after a walkthrough.
service_angles.sod-installation: When a Gilmer lawn has been scalped, burned out or overrun, sod is the clean restart. Sand lets roots move quickly, but it also lets water drain away, so we strip the old turf, work compost in to hold moisture, level the bed and lay Bermuda in sun or St. Augustine in shade. Sod is priced by the pallet, and most projects run $1,500 to $4,700.
service_angles.landscaping: Beds in sandy Gilmer soil drain well, which is good news for heat lovers like lantana, salvia and plumbago and bad news for anything thirsty. We build beds with compost worked in, pick plants that like it hot and dry, and lay out the yard so it is easy to keep up. Most projects run $900 to $3,600, and refreshes start at a few hundred dollars.
service_angles.flower-bed-installation: In Gilmer's sand, a new flower bed needs organic matter in it or it will dry out between every rain. We cut the bed shape, loosen and amend the soil, plant for the light the bed actually gets, and mulch it at the right depth. For a bare front bed, our $199 flower bed Design Preview shows you the layout before we plant anything.
service_angles.mulch-installation: Mulch does extra work on sandy ground: it slows evaporation and breaks down into the organic matter Gilmer soil is short on. We re-cut the edges, clean out the weeds by hand and lay hardwood 1 to 1.5 inches deep with no fabric under it, or pine straw if you like that look, ideally from late April to mid-May or in October. Most bed refreshes run $600 to $2,400.
service_angles.hardscaping: Gilmer's sandy soil drains well under a patio, but loose sand shifts if the base is not built and compacted right. We dig out, lay and compact a crushed stone base, and lock the edges so pavers and flagstone stay put, the same way for patios, walkways and fire pits. Most hardscape projects run $3,100 to $9,100.
service_angles.retaining-walls: Upshur County is rolling country, and a sandy slope washes fast when a heavy rain hits bare ground, so a low block or stone wall can hold a bed in place or flatten a spot for a patio. Every wall we build, short or tall, gets a compacted base, gravel backfill and a drain to daylight. Most walls run $3,000 to $19,000 by height and length.
service_angles.drainage: Sand drains fast, so drainage trouble in Gilmer usually comes down to a clay layer underneath, a low spot, a downspout dumping into a flat bed, or runoff cutting gullies through a sandy slope. We regrade, reroute downspouts, and install French drains and dry creek beds that move water to a real outlet. Most projects run $2,000 to $3,750.
service_angles.christmas-lights: Gilmer is an easy run from our shop, so standard light pricing applies, and most homes start at $900. We supply the lights, custom-cut C9 lines to fit your roofline, install them, take them down after the season and store them. Text us a photo of the house and we will quote it from a mock-up, in warm white or color.
service_angles.irrigation: Gilmer sand drains fast, which means a lawn can dry out in a few hot days. Even head-to-head coverage matters more here than almost anywhere, along with drip in the beds and a controller set for the summer, not for whenever the system went in.

lawn-maintenance.q: How short should I mow in Gilmer's sandy soil?
lawn-maintenance.a: Not short. Sandy ground dries out fast, and taller grass grows deeper roots and shades the soil. Keep Bermuda around two to two and a half inches in summer and St. Augustine at three and a half to four. Never take off more than a third of the blade in one mow.

leaf-removal.q: Can I just mow my leaves in Gilmer instead of hauling them?
leaf-removal.a: Early in the season, yes. Shredding the light October drop with the mower adds organic matter to sandy soil, which it needs. Once you cannot see grass after you mow, the leaves have to come up, especially off St. Augustine. That is when we switch to full cleanup and haul-off.

fertilization.q: How often should a Gilmer lawn be fertilized?
fertilization.a: We run four feedings a year on the East Texas schedule: late April, early July, early September and a potassium winterizer in late October. On sandy ground, slow-release product matters, because quick-release fertilizer washes through before the grass can use it. Feedings start from about $190 per visit.

hedge-trimming.q: How do you trim a long hedge along a driveway?
hedge-trimming.a: We shape it slightly wider at the bottom than the top so sun reaches the lower branches and the base stays full. The main shaping happens in early summer after the spring flush, with a light touch-up later if needed. Most hedge jobs run $150 to $800, and we haul off the clippings.

tree-shrub-care.q: When is the best time to prune trees and shrubs in Gilmer?
tree-shrub-care.a: Late winter, in February, for most trees and for crepe myrtles, while they are dormant. Spring bloomers like azaleas wait until right after they flower. We avoid heavy pruning in late summer, because the new growth will not harden off before the first freeze.

tree-planting.q: How do I keep a new tree alive in sandy soil?
tree-planting.a: Water the root ball, not the lawn. In sand the ball dries out fast, so soak it slowly twice a week for the first six weeks, then taper through winter. Plant in fall if you can, keep the root flare at grade, and keep a wide mulch ring pulled back off the trunk.

sod-installation.q: Does sod take in sandy soil around Gilmer?
sod-installation.a: It takes well if it gets water. Roots move through sand quickly, but the sod dries out just as fast, so it needs deep watering every morning for the first two weeks. We work compost in before laying so the soil holds moisture longer.

landscaping.q: What plants handle Gilmer's sandy soil?
landscaping.a: Plants that like it hot and well drained: lantana, salvia, plumbago, knockout roses and annual vinca in the sun, with hollies and wax myrtles for structure. We add compost to new beds so they hold water between rains without staying soggy.

flower-bed-installation.q: How much does a new flower bed cost in Gilmer?
flower-bed-installation.a: Most landscaping and planting projects run $900 to $3,600, and small refreshes start at a few hundred dollars. If you want to see the plan first, our flower bed Design Preview is $199, and the fee is credited toward the install if you book within 90 days.

mulch-installation.q: How deep should mulch be in Gilmer?
mulch-installation.a: About 1 to 1.5 inches of hardwood over a cleaned, edged bed. Deeper mulch sheds light rain and holds moisture against plant stems, which invites rot. In sandy soil, that thinner layer still slows evaporation and breaks down into organic matter the bed needs.

hardscaping.q: What kind of patio works best on sandy ground?
hardscaping.a: Pavers or flagstone both work if the base is right. We dig out the loose sand, build a compacted crushed stone base, and lock the edges so nothing creeps. Most patio projects run $3,100 to $9,100, depending on size, material and access.

retaining-walls.q: Do short garden walls need drainage too?
retaining-walls.a: Yes. Even a two-foot wall holds back wet soil after a heavy rain. We put gravel backfill and a drain behind every wall we build, short or tall, so water does not build pressure and push it out of line.

drainage.q: My Gilmer yard is sandy. Why does it still hold water?
drainage.a: Sand on top often sits on clay underneath. Water soaks through the sand fast, hits the clay and stops, so low spots stay wet. We look at the grade and where the water collects, then fix it with regrading, a French drain or a swale that moves it to an outlet.

christmas-lights.q: When should I book Christmas lights in Gilmer?
christmas-lights.a: Booking opens in early October, and the earlier you call, the better your install date. Most homes start at $900. Send us a photo of the house and we will put together a mock-up and quote without needing to come out first.

irrigation.q: Do you install sprinkler systems in Gilmer?
irrigation.a: Yes. We install and repair sprinkler systems in Gilmer and around Upshur County, under a Texas licensed irrigator, and pull the permit the job requires. It's about 25 miles up Highway 300 from Longview, and the walkthrough is free.
